Oracle Database options / SAP indirect access / IBM sub-capacity

compliance_entities.basis: Effective License Position (ELP) is the contractually-defined reconciliation publishers demand at audit. Non-optional in any SAM that defends an audit.
The bundle of deployment + entitlement proof submitted in a publisher audit. Required artifact of an audit response.
Documented over/under-deployment gaps from a reconciliation; the exposure record. Named license_audit_findings (NOT audit_findings) to avoid catalog collision with FSQM audit_findings (id 294).
Annual contractual true-up (Microsoft EA, Adobe ETLA, etc.) reconciling actual vs entitled consumption; a financial+compliance record.
Formal response letter and negotiation record returned to the publisher; the defensible audit-engagement artifact.
The settlement / remediation purchase resulting from an audit; closes the exposure with a contractual obligation.
ISO/IEC 19770-2 SWID tags are the standardized, publisher-issued identification artifact underpinning trustworthy entitlement recognition.

missing.reason: The software publisher (Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, Adobe, SAP) is a first-class master in every flagship; titles, licenses, audits and use-rights all hang off it. Currently absent.
Effective License Position is the central computed output of SAM (entitled vs consumed per metric). The whole entitlement module exists to produce it; today there is no entity to hold it.

License metric (per-core, per-user, PVU, named-user, concurrent) is the unit of measure for reconciliation. Without it software_licenses cannot be reconciled against installations. Core in Flexera/Snow/USU/ServiceNow.
The aggregated pool of purchased rights that installations draw down against. The reconciliation join surface; modeled in all four big platforms.
Metered actual usage of installed software (last-used, peak concurrent) drives reclamation and metric-based true-ups. SAM-METER capability has no backing entity today.
Annual contractual true-up reconciliation (EA/ETLA). A compliance + financial record with no home today.
The evidence bundle submitted in a publisher audit. license_audits has no child evidence/finding/response structure; audit defense is a single bare master today.
The per-product gap/exposure record produced by an audit. Compliance core; use SAM-specific name to avoid collision with FSQM audit_findings (294).
The formal publisher response/letter and negotiation record. The audit-engagement transaction; absent today.
Edition (Standard/Enterprise/Datacenter) drives licensing rules independently of title; normalization is edition-aware in every catalog. Missing.
Version is the EOL/EOSL and downgrade-rights pivot. Missing.
The rules that map raw discovered inventory to normalized titles/editions/versions. The core IP of a SAM catalog (Flexera Technopedia, ServiceNow Content Library). Missing.
A discrete inventory/discovery execution producing installation records. The SAM-DISCOVERY capability has no transaction entity. Missing.
Configured inventory connectors (agents, SCCM/Intune, scanners) feeding discovery. Missing.
The license model/type taxonomy (perpetual, subscription, OEM, CAL, capacity). Common config master.
Activation/product keys and entitlement certificates. Common in Snow/ServiceNow/Certero.
Junction allocating entitlement to org_units/devices/installations. The reconciliation linkage. Missing.
User-to-license assignment for named-user/subscription metrics. Drives compliance for per-user licensing. Missing.
Harvesting of unused installs back to the pool (driven by usage_meterings). Optimization core; missing.
On-prem maintenance/support renewal of a software_license (distinct from SMP saas_subscription renewals). SAM-RENEWAL capability has no entity.
Point-in-time compliant/non-compliant posture per publisher, distilled from ELP. The board-level reporting artifact. Missing.
Downgrade/second-use/BYOL/virtualization use rights that change effective entitlement. Specialist (Flexera/USU/ServiceNow). Missing.
ISO/IEC 19770-2 SWID tags - the standardized identification artifact for trustworthy recognition. Specialist/compliance.
Functional categorization of titles (used for spend grouping and policy). Common config.
End-of-life / end-of-support dates per version that drive risk and renewal. Common config.

Publisher-specific add-on entitlement structures (Oracle DB options/packs, SAP indirect-access, IBM sub-capacity). Specialist (USU/Flexera). One generic master rather than vendor-named entities (Rule #18).
The remediation/settlement purchase that closes an audit exposure. Compliance; absent.

sam_smp_boundary.observation: On-prem licensing ends and SaaS management begins at the asset type, and the catalog already enforces the split cleanly. SAM masters software_titles/software_installations/software_licenses (installed, perpetual/subscription on-prem, metric-based reconciliation, publisher audit). SMP masters saas_applications/saas_subscriptions/saas_usage_metrics (cloud-hosted, seat-based, renewal & optimization). NO entity is currently duplicated as a domain_owned master across both: SMP's seat/usage/renewal entities are all smp_*-prefixed and saas_*-named, distinct from SAM's software_*/license_* names.

shared_embedded_masters.verdict: PASS - both embed the CLM master; correct shape, not duplication
PASS - both embed the HCM master; correct shape, not duplication

watch_items.guidance: SAM-proposed license_renewals must scope to on-prem maintenance/support renewal of a software_license. SaaS subscription renewal stays in SMP (smp_renewal_engagements/smp_renewal_tasks). Keep names distinct (license_renewals vs smp_renewal_*) and do NOT add a saas_subscription-shaped renewal to SAM. Already respected by naming.

SAM usage_meterings = installed-software metering (last-used, concurrent, metric counters for reconciliation). SMP saas_usage_metrics = SaaS login/seat-activity telemetry. Distinct concepts, distinct names. No collision, but flag so a future load does not collapse them into one shared master.

modularization.commentary: The 3-module split is coherent and self-explaining for a first-time deployer: catalog+discovery (what software exists and where it is installed), entitlement (what we are licensed for and reconciliation), audit defense (proving it to a publisher). Each module has >=1 domain_owned master (Rule #14 satisfied). The split mirrors how Flexera/Snow/ServiceNow segment their own UIs (Inventory/Discovery vs Licenses/Entitlements vs Compliance/Audit). The 25 MISSING masters all fit one of the three existing modules WITHOUT requiring new modules - the previously-proposed 6-module re-split (SAM-METERING, SAM-RENEWAL as standalone modules) is NOT required by the surface: metering/renewal are sub-capabilities of entitlement management, and every flagship packages them inside the license/entitlement product, not as separate products. Recommendation: KEEP 3 modules; load the missing masters into the existing three. The only judgment call worth surfacing is whether ELP/metering/renewal grow large enough later to warrant splitting SAM-ENTITLEMENT-MGMT into entitlement vs optimization (mirrors SMP-OPTIMIZATION being separate from SMP-RENEWAL-VENDOR), but that is a later scaling decision, not a present defect.

recommendations.reason: 3 modules coherently cover the full vendor surface; all 25 missing masters slot into an existing module; no empty modules; Rule #14 satisfied. Supersedes the 2026-05-30 6-module proposal (B2-S1).

If usage_meterings + license_reclamations + license_position_calculations grow into a distinct optimization workflow (as SMP split SMP-OPTIMIZATION from SMP-RENEWAL-VENDOR), consider splitting later. NOT required now; entitlement module currently holds only 1 master and would carry ~13 after the load, which is still a coherent single module. Surface as a future scaling note, not a present fix.
